notes.title: 'The Ghost Ship' survival mode and 'Jolly Roger' casual mode added!
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy there Sea Rats![/h2]

It’s been quite some time since our last post but we’re super excited to launch a big content update today just in time to celebrate the [b]Steam Spring sale![/b]

This new content drop includes two brand-new game modes, balance changes to the in-game economy system, enhanced enemy and boss behaviour patterns, improved UI and map quality of life, two additional VO languages, and minor bug and achievement fixes! There’s a lot to cover, so read on for a breakdown of what's included. 

NOTE: This update is currently live on all versions EXCEPT for Nintendo Switch! We expect the Switch version to be updated in the next week or so, thanks for your patience!

[h3]New gameplay mode: ‘Jolly Roger’ (casual) mode[/h3]

The first of the two new game modes has been designed to address player feedback relating to the game’s difficulty and cater to a more casual play experience. The ‘Jolly Roger’ mode can be selected when you begin a new story campaign OR any time you change character when visiting Wu Yun during a campaign. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/91bfcf6519560f8af05f83a8656f985897d05824.png[/img]

This mode makes the following significant changes to the core gameplay:   
[list]
[*] Contact damage has been removed so you will only receive damage from enemies when they attack you. To complement this, most enemies no longer block your movement and can be passed through.
[*] Enemies only respawn in rooms if you interact with Wu Yun. This means that you can explore the environment more freely, and can no longer farm enemies by immediately re-entering cleared rooms. 
[*] You can now warp to unlocked ancestral doors from anywhere on the map and are therefore no longer required to backtrack to specific rooms.
[*] All enemies have reduced health.
[*] Player characters inflict more damage. 
[/list]
[h3]New gameplay mode: ‘The Ghost Ship’ (wave survival) mode[/h3]

On the flip side, the second game mode introduces a much more challenging experience in the form of an arcade-style wave survival mode that should appeal to players who love classic beat ‘em ups and racing against the clock! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/b2d252259424b53094dd5a62d322ae5de1beb809.gif[/img]

‘The Ghost Ship’ mode can be selected directly from the main menu and features: 
[list]
[*] 1-4 players must fight to clear 10 waves, with each wave consisting of a wide variety of enemies and bosses from the main story. Special abilities such as double jump and air dash are unlocked by default and will be essential for avoiding taking damage within such a confined space.   
[*] Once a wave has been cleared, pick between 3 different stat buffs or powerful items to increase your chances of survival. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/ed5d4577aa87465b01d939578368d95f61a3dc5b.png[/img]

[*] After certain ‘milestone’ waves you’ll also unlock additional bonuses in the form of new ‘inner element’ magical abilities and magic slots. But be warned, however, if all players are defeated progress will be lost!  
[*] Your fastest clear times will be logged after each wave so you can challenge yourself to smash your existing records!
[/list]
If the challenge proves too much you can also play ‘The Ghost Ship’ using the ‘Jolly Roger Mode settings.

[h3]Enemy bestiary[/h3]

We received a lot of requests for an enemy bestiary to be added to help complete ‘The Fighter’ achievement which requires you to defeat one of each enemy. A bestiary can now be accessed via the inventory menu once you have obtained the Explorer Goggles by defeating Rama Cinnamon and Banana and keeps a running tally of every enemy that you have defeated so far in your adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/065ae9c77c817a623f9a9aebb2e7d08ee788424a.png[/img]

[h3]Balance changes[/h3]

In response to community feedback we’ve made the following balance changes:
[list]
[*] Gold and spiritual energy economies have been rebalanced.
[*] Enemies core stats have been rebalanced.
[*] All bosses have had their behavior patterns and animations adjusted to create more engaging boss fights. It is now much clearer which attack they will make and there is more time for you to react.
[/list]
[h3]UI and map changes[/h3]

We made some small changes to the UI and map:
[list]
[*] Tweaks to the UI and map background changes
[*] A new gate room has been added close to where you encounter Dolores. 
[/list]
[h3]Additional voiceover languages[/h3]

Alongside the full English VO, we have added Catalan and Spanish voice acting reflecting our heritage as a Barcelona-based studio! 

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]

Finally, we have squashed the following bugs:
[list]
[*] Fixed bug with Cocoon debuff.
[*] Fixed Gunner VFX not ending properly.
[*] Fixed missing map icons. 
[*] Fixed audio issues when quickly changing scenes. 
[*] Fixed the initial cutscene not working on Steam Deck. 
[*] Fixed visual bug when a box falls above a player. 
[*] Fixed teleportation bug when other players change scenes. 
[*] Fixed VFX not disappearing after scene change. 
[*] Fixed incorrect dialogues in certain situations. 
[*] Adjusted the volume of some sound effects. 
[*] Fixed Necromancer not reappearing in some cases.
[*] Fixed Morrigan being able to take damage while invulnerable. 
[*] Improved legibility of some notification text.
[*] Fixed spirit counter showing incorrect numbers upon first appearance. 
[*] Fixed minimap does not reappear after the boss fights in some cases. 
[*] Fixed hitbox for Gunner enemy. 
[*] Fixed projectiles do not work when enemies are electrocuted. 
[*] Fixed movement during cutscenes. 
[*] Fixed audio issues when blocking Specter. 
[*] Fixed an issue where Freddy’s mini spiders didn’t appear. 
[*] Adjusted font size across all UI elements.
[*] Fixed enemies sometimes do not deal damage.
[*] Fixed InkTopus death animation. 
[*] Fixed issues with effects UI. 
[*] Fixed Skull Thrower player detection. 
[*] Fixed bug when skipping Granny Malone’s dialogue. 
[*] Fixed several shader issues. 
[*] Fixed some debuffs not hiding in the UI. 
[*] Fixed Bussa block. 
[*] Fixed issue when dashing after a dash attack. 
[*] Fixed Morrigan’s VFX not disappearing in some cases.
[*] Fixed the issue where Leprechaun didn’t reappear after failing the minigame.
[*] Fixed the hitbox of Banana Tucan not flipping correctly.
[*] Fixed a bug when disconnecting the controller in a room with a different FOV. 
[*] Fixed issue with controller vibration not stopping. 
[*] Fixed The Fighter trophy unlocks.
[*] Fixed delay when opening the inventory on some platforms. 
[*] Fixed bug when opening the map while running.
[/list]
Thank you all for your continued support, we really hope you’ll enjoy the new content and improvements we have made. The Steam Spring sale runs from [b]13th - 20th March[/b] and we’ll be running a [u][b]massive 65% discount[/b][/u] on Curse of the Sea Rats for the duration of the event, so now is the perfect time to grab some mates and jump in 🙂

notes.title: Free 'The Ghost Ship' survival mode update coming soon!
notes.content:
[h3]Welcome back Sea Rats![/h3]

We’re excited to share with you our upcoming plans for the [b]upcoming 1.4.0 patch[/b] as well as reveal a FREE content drop which adds an entirely [b]new gameplay mode![/b]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1bd5a1951421c1f895c5243064d1293cd0ce5dbd.png[/img]

Thank you all for the love and support so far with [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i], your feedback has helped us implement three waves of updates so far including:
[list]
[*] [b]1.0.2:[/b] Rebalanced Character Skills and Robert Garfield’s Store Prices for a smoother and fairer experience along with several bug fixes
[*] [b]1.1.2:[/b] More bug fixes and changes to the late-game progression and final sequence to make the experience feel less grind-y.
[*] [b]1.3.7:[/b] Major improvements to the combat system including animation cancelling, improved hitbox detection, more dynamic and responsive platforming, disabled pitfall deaths, improved Map UI, and so many more quality-of-life changes!
[/list]
The improvements won’t stop there, as mentioned we are now working towards the next big patch, 1.4.0. This update will add an [b]enemy log menu[/b] to showcase which enemies (and how many of them) the player has defeated, [b]improvements to the player inventory UI[/b], and additional changes to [b]boss balancing.[/b] 1.4.0 is scheduled to go live later this Summer.

This brings us to an exciting announcement, we’re currently putting the finishing touches on a [b]Major Free Content Update![/b] [i][b]“The Ghost Ship” [/b][/i]adds a new [b]Survival Mode[/b] that tasks players with defeating increasingly more challenging waves of enemies and bosses one after another!

If the player(s) can clear a wave they will receive a reward in the form of a usable item, attack or defence buff before progressing onto the next wave. After certain ‘milestone’ waves player characters will also unlock additional bonuses in the form of new ‘inner element’ magical abilities and skills. But be warned however, if all players are defeated progress will be lost! 

When playing through [i][b]The Ghost Ship[/b][/i] your fastest clear times will be logged after each wave so you can challenge yourself to smash your existing records!  

How far will you progress against such terrifying odds? [i][b]The Ghost Ship[/b][/i] update is planned for Fall 2023.

Finally, if you’re enjoying Curse of the Sea Rats please consider leaving a positive review? We’re working hard to respond to as much player feedback as possible and add exciting new content to make the experience the very best it can be. 

Until next time!

Petoons Studio

notes.title: Curse of the Sea Rats is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[h2]Avast ye![/h2] 

The wait is finally over, [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] is OUT NOW! The time has come to take down Flora Burn, rescue Admiral Blacksmith’s son, and reverse the curse once and for all!  

Check out the action-packed Launch Trailer below:

[previewyoutube=iPZwoGoNOkA;full][/previewyoutube]

Play as one of [b]four prisoners of the British Empire[/b] on their quest for freedom and utilise their newly awakened [b]elemental powers.[/b] Harness fire with the swash-buckling [b]David Douglas[/b], unleash lightning-fast combos as [b]Buffalo Calf[/b], create catastrophic quakes as [b]Bussa[/b], or harness the devastating power of a tsunami as [b]Akane Yamakawa[/b].  

Battle your way through hordes of pirates, fauna, and flora to gain [b]Spiritual Energy[/b], and visit [b]Wu Yun[/b] to unlock new abilities and upgrade your skills. 

Explore a [b]huge variety of different environments[/b] along the Irish Coast and take on [b]challenging bosses.[/b] Seek out a [b]range of NPCs[/b] including fellow shipwrecked crew, eccentric locals and even supernatural entities. Embark on [b]numerous side quests[/b] and uncover the mysteries of the Island... 

[b]Team up in 2-4 player local coop[/b] or utilise [b]Steam Remote Play Together to link up online![/b] To learn more about the Steam Remote Play Together process [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3683422028778962952][b]CLICK HERE. [/b][/url]

Before you get started, we’ve also put together a handy FAQ that should answer the most frequently asked questions you might have about [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats:[/b][/i] 

[b]Q. Is there multiplayer? [/b]

[b]A.[/b] You can play co-operatively with 2-4 players in local multiplayer and Steam Remote Play Together. 

[b]Q. What controller options are there for multiplayer mode? [/b]

[b]A.[/b] Player 1 can use a keyboard or controller, however all additional players must use a controller, this also applies to Steam Remote Play Together.  

[b]Q. Are there custom key bindings?[/b] 

[b]A.[/b] There are limited custom key bindings. 

Movement controls will not be customisable and will remain as W,A,S,D or ←,↑,→,↓ 

However, the following will be customisable: 
[list]
[*] Jump 
[*] Attack 
[*] Dash 
[*] Magic ability  
[*] Technique  
[*] Map 
[/list]
Instructions on how to customise key bindings are as follows: In-game -> Pause Menu -> Controls -> Press ENTER -> Select KEY(s) to change -> ENTER -> Input new KEY 

[b]Q. How long is the game?[/b] 

[b]A.[/b] 10+ hours but this will vary depending on the number of players and their skill levels! 

[b]Q. Are there multiple endings? [/b]

[b]A.[/b] Yes, there are 4 endings (one of which is secret, sshhh!) 

[i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] is out now!

[h2]Ahoy Sea Rats![/h2]

There’s only one more week to go until the release of [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats![/b][/i] While we countdown the days until you embark on your adventure, we’d like to take this opportunity to re-introduce the playable characters; David Douglas, Buffalo Calf, Bussa, and Akana Yamakawa as well as some of the nefarious bosses that you'll be facing! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1431cd3a80fb233b00efd5e7e5b3d4108b64c0d3.png[/img]

Remember it’s not just Flora’s scurvy crew that you’ll be battling, the pirate-witch’s corrupting magic has also spread to the local fauna!

[previewyoutube=GHnDFkc2Rto;full][/previewyoutube]

Take on over 16 challenging bosses with up to three friends in local 4-player co-op or utilise [b]Steam Remote Play[/b] to team-up online!

After booting up [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] you will be prompted by Steam to access Steam Remote Play. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/62e9982ca1677fe22e9c9d1c53a00174958f1c59.png[/img]

Then, to Host a session, click on either Invite a Friend to have an existing Steam friend join or Invite a Guest to share a link to someone not on your friends list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/c0958a5f395ea8ad0c724186f46dc5bdacf63c69.png[/img]

And that’s it! Once you load into a game just have your co-op party press the prompted Join button and embark on your new adventure, together.

notes.title: Developer Interview Part 2 - Crafting the Characters
notes.content:
[h2]Avast ye Sea Rats![/h2]

With just 2 weeks to go until [b]Curse of the Sea Rats launches on 6th April [/b]we’ve prepared another developer interview with some of the key staff from Petoons Studio! If you missed [b]Part 1: 'Building the World'[/b] you can check it out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3658650327115173441][b]HERE.[/b][/url]

Today we'll be looking at [b]Part 2: ‘Crafting the Characters’[/b] where we shine the spotlight on character and boss design, animation techniques, and voice acting! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/11e62579da4fbc13dce3e99690d4c11fadfbee30.png[/img]

[h3]Character & Boss Design with Lead Game Designer, Yeray Toledano and Senior Game Designer, Alex Calvo. [/h3]

[b]Q: Can you tell us a bit about the process of designing the 4 playable heroes? [/b]  

[b]Yeray:[/b] David Douglas was the first character we developed. He was the first one we talked about and the first character to be created. He’s the most balanced character, both in offensive and defensive capabilities and is the ideal character to start with if you are not sure which combat style you like the most. Douglas is basically for everyone! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/bd6113546c85a4cb3d7faeac5e3d01935366593d.gif[/img]

[b]Alex:[/b] It was important to us from the beginning, that each character had to play differently and have a unique role in combat. Buffalo Calf is unique compared to the rest of the Sea Rats, since she has a lot of ranged abilities and is extremely fast and nimble.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f8f2fd144ab10146bc042898309f5a1a58365b2b.gif[/img]

[b]Yeray:[/b] She can also become invisible, throw elemental projectiles, and execute multi-directional ariel attacks… In contrast, Douglas has only his mid-range pistol and fire attacks. Each of the characters is tied to an element, Douglas uses his firearms to channel his magic, while Buffalo harnesses electricity through her throwing knives and tomahawks.  

[b]Alex:[/b] Then, as a counterpoint, we have Bussa. He is the tankiest character by far, with more hit points than the other heroes. Instead of a parry ability, Bussa can hold his block and stay on guard for a while. We also think he’s the friendliest of the four characters (laughs). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/797aa8ba39be343d4d563634d2c43549f7ae4ffd.gif[/img]

[b]Yeray:[/b] While his attacks are slow, they do quite a bit of damage! Bussa’s gameplay style embodies his inner element, which is Earth, so on the outside he’s hard like granite! But despite this he does have a softer and more sensitive side which you’ll hopefully see as the adventure progresses. 

Then we have Akane, the youngest and also the smallest! But beware, as a warrior of the shogun she’s pretty fierce and has some of the strongest attacks in the game! 

Akane is quite agile but has less physical resistance to damage and as a result loses health quickly. She ultimately puts everything into her attack and uses versatile water magic to overcome the enemy. You’ll notice that her movements and combos are really fluid, just like her inner element, Water! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/d111f308aa33599705e616eaf199423ef1ebbc5b.gif[/img]

Throughout the game, you will unlock different kinds of magical abilities for each character. For example, one of Akane’s skills adds a water projectile to her aeriel attacks, while another creates a water shield which protects her and simultaneously damages nearby enemies. She’s a really cool character and plays aggressively! 

[b]Q: Could you tell us more about the design of Flora Burn and her crewmates? [/b]

[b]Yeray:[/b] We're not going to say too much about Flora Burn because she's an important character and we haven't seen much of her yet in previous trailers and demos, but suffice to say she uses A LOT of magic! We can’t forget that she was already a pirate witch before her encounter with the Eye of the Serpent, so she is extremely powerful in that sense and uses it to her advantage with premeditation and treachery. 

Flora is cunning, like a snake, and uses the power of the serpent to her advantage. She’s charismatic, with a lot of personality and a peculiar way of interacting with her subordinates. She's also deceitful, tricky, mocking, and her magic and combat style reflect this, so don’t let her deceive you! 

In a weird way Flora is almost like a parent figure amongst her crew. Not because she is affectionate, but because she has to put up with their nonsense and make sure they stay focused! She sees herself as being surrounded by incompetence, which isn’t entirely wrong! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/2edef83bfe422ec112e9ad7c89212e68702d74b9.png[/img]

[b]Alex:[/b] Regarding Flora’s crew, there are personalities of all types in the mix. Some characters are mysterious like the vampiric Murat Reis and sinister Freddy Eightfingers, while others provide some comic relief, such as the uptight Short Fuse Jones and ponderous Fatso. We also have the sultry Rama Cinnamon and her companion Sharpie The Sharp, who share a close relationship. There are different dynamics amongst Flora’s crew, and you’ll witness a few bust-ups because of their clashing personalities. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/076f6165a74123764546da7282fa0a323d3f37ce.jpg[/img]

[b]Q: How are the boss battles presented to the player?[/b]

[b]Yeray:[/b] They’re all really varied! One of the more unique boss battles is Rama Cinammon, who has two phases: During the first phase she’s really agile employing a mixture of close-range melee attacks with her whip, and long range attacks with her vines.  And then, in the second phase she teams up with her pet toucan Banana, and begins to attack from above using air currents to sweep the heroes off the treetops of Eriu’s Forest! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/2ea3c3ee42404bae4c71491a7aba524260274aae.gif[/img]

[b]Alex:[/b] On the island, there are not only the pirates, but also local inhabitants and fauna such as the Lighthouse Keeper, Krabawaki, La Chusa, Necromancer... (the coolest character of all!) And some other mysteries that you’ll have to discover. Each boss has a really different style of combat accompanied by some truly expressive hand-drawn animations!  

[b]Q: What can you tell is about the process of designing boss battles?[/b]

[b]Yeray:[/b] Designing a Boss battle is actually one of the more complex processes, you always start with an idea, a concept or something you want to teach the player. Thinking about the main objective that you want to achieve with that boss: visually, the movement, the attack patterns... and that's how the central plan is designed. 

For example, if I want to highlight the jump mechanic, the boss is going to be designed around this. The game’s first boss, Fatso was designed exactly for this purpose: we wanted to teach the player how to move, jump, and dodge... To get a little used to the enemies that were going to come later. And well, basically we started by making some attack ideas and thinking about which objective could be achieved by each individual attack. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/c34f3214396ee18a40f17a36d9ed5090c258dd3c.gif[/img]

[b]Alex:[/b] When Fatso throws his barrels or propels himself forwards, the player must time their jumps differently. We always start with drawings or schematics with detailed descriptions of the attacks, then this passes into the hands of Concept Artists who make a first sketch of what the characters will look like during these moments. 

We get a lot of feedback from the Concept Artists: we propose things to them and then they respond, and so a boss character is built collaboratively between the two teams.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1363773a47486977289e48f753429f97e1740a1b.png[/img]

The Animation department are actually amazing, and they have some super crazy and fun ideas. Once we have the description of the attacks from the Game Designers, and the visuals of the boss from the Concept Artists, the Animators begin work on the animations for all of the attacks! 

After this stage the Programmers work on the Boss AI. This way, we can test it and give our feedback to see if things like timings need to be changed. Most importantly we get a feel for the boss’s movement speed and how many frames have to be drawn for each attack. 

[b]Yeray:[/b] As we test and tweak, we can soon see which attacks have to do more damage. We also played around a lot with the level of the characters, that is, scaling boss difficulty to the level where the characters are, and the skills that are likely to be unlocked at the point of encounter.  

[h3]2D Animation techniques with Lead Animator, Al Díaz and Senior Animator, Guillem Vallhonrat[/h3]    

[b]Q: Could you tell us about your approach to animation?[/b] 

[b]Al:[/b] The style of the characters in Curse of the Sea Rats is quite cartoonish, and stylized, therefore the animations needed to match accordingly. We also took into account that this is a video game and not a film, so tiny details needed to look good and the character movements had to stand out and be easily understood by the player. 

[b]Guillem:[/b] Once the Concept Artists finish designing the characters, the Game Designers define the movesets and give us a completed animation concept. First, we make an initial sketch, where you can only see a bit of the silhouette of the character, and we test it in the game to see how it looks and how the timings feel. Does it go too fast, too slow, or look does it look small? Once we get this feeling right, we go through the rough phase adding in the facial features, the actions and the details of the character’s clothing which we'll later clean up! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/df50d33ffa536db68ab2384596f7c47194c794b0.gif[/img]

[b]Q: Was there a character that you really enjoyed working on?[/b]

[b]Al:[/b] The Lighthouse Keeper was the first boss I animated and I'm fond of him because I had to think about all his different attacks. I really focused on varying his movements and animations in the later phases of the fight to really ramp up the tension and let the player know that things were getting serious! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/9875885dcaecf53d6161cd6b24fa992a9f198461.gif[/img]

[b]Q: Did you face any challenges?[/b] 

[b]Guillem:[/b] For some attacks and movements that were particularly difficult to animate we used video references as a guide. Thankfully, the fact that the game has such a cartoony style, meant that we were able to exaggerate everything and add lots of additional colour. This gave us the freedom to do deformations and things that a more realistic art-style just wouldn’t have allowed. 

[h3]Recording the voiceover with Game Director, Dani del Amor & Lead Game Designer, Yeray Toledano[/h3] 

[b]Q: Tell us about the voiceover recording process?[/b] 

[b]Dani:[/b] For the voice dubbing we hired a professional UK-based studio called Charactoons, who previously worked on Disco Elysium, a game that we loved! It has honestly been such a pleasure working with them. 

Studio Owner Mikee has been a real star throughout the project, and was instrumental in finding all the actors and actresses. He’s also really fun to work with! 

[b]Yeray:[/b] Importantly, Charactoons helped us find diverse actors from a wide variety of backgrounds. Since we have characters representing different nationalities, genres, and ages the voice actors had to be authentic to their on-screen counterparts. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/17dee340dd1ac4d310f8d52582920b980004ba7f.png[/img]

To begin with, we looked for reference actors to link with each character. We passed these references to Charactoons to see if they could find similar voices and match the appropriate nationalities.  

They then gave us different tests with different actors, all of them are talented and cool, so it was really hard picking our favorites! After that we started the dubbing. 

[b]Dani:[/b] In Curse of the Sea Rats there are characters representing all sorts of nationalities (e.g. Spanish, Japanese, American English etc...). Given the game’s setting we had to take great care with all of the regional accents for British and Irish characters in particular! You’ll discover characters who are clearly Irish, Scottish, and Welsh, but you’ll also hear specific regional accents being represented. It really breathes life and a sense of authenticity into the game! 

[b]Yeray:[/b] During the dubbing process, Dani was present in the studio. It was a cool experience! We had previously done some recording for other games but never at this scale. It was enriching because there were people here working in Barcelona alongside the team in the UK and everyone was collaborating to make sure that we didn't miss any lines of dialogue, and that everything was shot in the right context... When you're recording, you do takes with each individual character separately and some context can be lost against the conversation that actually takes place in the game. Different characters are interacting with one another depending on the context, so the actors had to be careful to preserve the tone of the conversation! In the final cut, we felt that they were all coherent and fun, transmitting the emotion that was originally intended. 

[b]Dani:[/b] Some alterations to the script were also made in the studio because when the actor or actress gets into character, they naturally make contributions. So, maybe a phrase that worked well in the script, doesn’t work in practice and then the actor makes a better suggestion during the performance. If it fits, then you write it down and make the appropriate amendments in-game! 

[b]Q: How did you pick the best takes and do you have any favourite performances?[/b]

[b]Dani:[/b] (Laughs) It’s really difficult to choose a favourite take because everyone did great and I think that every reading offers something interesting and unique. It’s true that when there are actors or actresses who have lots of experience, when they do four takes, all four sound good. 

I also preferred interpretations that surprised me, Mikee Goodman’s rendition of the Serpent was amazing as you can hear a snake’s hiss within his voice! I honestly didn't think it was possible for a human being to make these sounds... 

[b]Yeray:[/b] Another favourite of mine was Flora, the dubbing actress added a lot to the character. It gave her so much personality, a bit like Cruella de Vil: evil but elegant at the same time. 

[b]Dani:[/b] I found it interesting to see that some voice actors were able to perform as multiple characters. In some cases, the same actor plays two characters that are going to interact in the same conversation and makes them sound totally different. When you hear these two characters talking to each other in-game they sound like two separate people. It's awesome! 

That's all for today and remember, [b]Curse of the Sea Rats launches on 6th April 2023! [/b]

Petoons Studio

notes.title: Developer Interview Part 1 - Building the World
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy there![/h2]

With just 4 weeks to go until [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] launches on [u][b]6th April[/b][/u] we’ve prepared an exclusive 2 part interview with some of the key member of the Petoons Studio team!

Today we’ll be introducing [b]Part 1: ‘Building the world’[/b] where we take a look at the game concept and core inspiration, environmental design, and original soundtrack! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/840fa8ae04c9b6c541fde73dab71e29882ba9c05.png[/img]

[h3]Game Direction & Narrative Design with Game Director, Dani del Amor. [/h3]

[b]Q: Can you tell us about the core concept of the game and its main characters? [/b]

[b]Dani:[/b] Curse of the Sea Rats is a classic Metroidvania, but with a strong narrative component. Aside from what would be typical Metroidvania elements like combat and exploration, you will find yourself empathizing a lot with the character you choose. You’ll also discover many side characters throughout the game, and by interacting with them will learn more about their backstories and needs. With this, we also try to make you smile from time to time, humor is a key part of the game! 

[b]Q: What can you tell us about the incident on board the HMS Barfleur and Flora Burn’s plan? [/b]

[b]Dani:[/b] The game begins with the British ship, HMS Barfleur, returning to England from the Caribbean with a hold full of prisoners. Among these prisoners are our protagonists, four individuals each with their own unique backstories. While they are not necessarily common criminals, they are lawbreakers in the eyes of the British Empire, and must stand trial for their crimes. Imprisoned alongside them is the notorious pirate captain Flora Burn, who possesses a mysterious ancient artefact, the Eye of the Serpent, that she stole (in a part of the story that is not going to be revealed now). She uses this artefact to turn all the Barfleur’s crew and its prisoners into rats, allowing her to escape along with her nefarious crew. And this is where the game begins. 

[b]Q: So what exactly is the Eye of the Serpent and who is Flora Burn?[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/5b88b48ababc41de4e4db563203fc73fc7465f39.png[/img]

[b]Dani:[/b] The Eye of the Serpent is comprised of an amulet and a ring. To recover their human form, the prisoners must reunite these pieces in order to invoke the artefact’s power again and reverse the curse. The artefact is a kind of “magic lamp”, with a spirit inside that grants wishes. But at the same time, it embodies the concept of yin and yang, of good and evil. When both pieces are together they allow you to fulfil any wish. But when separated, good and evil are no longer balanced. The amulet is the good half where Wu Yun, the heroes’ guide, resides. The ring is the evil half, possessed by a serpentine spirit that Flora Burn uses to increase her magical powers!

However, Flora Burn is not inherently evil. She’s a pirate captain who travels the Caribbean and does what she pleases, and her life philosophy means that she won’t bow to any state, to any government, living in freedom.

Her objective is fundamentally to recover this freedom, return to the Caribbean and continue with her treasure hunting and raids on the ships of the British Empire and its various outposts. Unfortunately, our main characters happen to cross paths with her at exactly the wrong time, and although they share some values, they end up in direct conflict with her goals! 

[b]Q: Who are the main heroes of the game and how does their gameplay differ?[/b] 

[b]Dani:[/b] Starting with David Douglas, he is the most balanced character. An individual who does everything reasonably well, but does not stand out in any particular field. He’s a character with no defined fighting style and as such is a good choice for the beginner! He's your typical adventure hero, while the other three characters have more clearly defined roles and gameplay styles. 

For example, Buffalo Calf is much more agile and is designed to fight from a distance. This gives her a distinct playstyle, fun for players who enjoy ariel acrobatics and fast combos! During battles, this allows you to play at a distance and therefore avoid taking damage. 

Bussa, on the other hand, is a tank through and through. He’s a character that is designed to inflict a lot of physical damage at close range, which exposes him to the majority of incoming damage. 

Akane Yamakawa is a complex and versatile character, with slightly more range because of her naginata, and decent amount of agility. When she executes a successful combo this can be really destructive. She is almost a perfect mix of the other three characters, but that's just my opinion!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/22fe1807ef0825af2b90b69e19c82e7976a72fd9.gif[/img]

Admiral Blacksmith is a stoic figure, who gives the prisoners their mission. He is an individual who is fiercely loyal to his country, to his family, and to his crew... He is that person who tries to do everything right, but the world seems to be intent on making this difficult for him. 

At the start of the game he is on a mission to transport the prisoners to England, with his son accompanying him. During the journey, everything goes wrong and his son is kidnapped by Flora. Of course, he cannot abandon his ship and crew to pursue the pirate-witch, so must place his trust in our 4 heroes to embark on the rescue mission…

[h3]Art direction & environmental design with Lead Concept Artist, Xavi Montell, Senior Concept Artist, Júlia Fernández and 3D Artist, Enric Trullols.[/h3] 

[b]Q: Can you tell us about the inspiration behind the art direction and game world? [/b]

[b]Xavi:[/b] Curse of the Sea Rats is largely inspired by Don Bluth’s animated adventure films that emerged in the 1980s and 1990s, such as “The Secret of NIMH”, “Pebble and the Penguin”, “The Land Before Time”. Naturally, movies starring mice and rats such as "The Rescuers" and "The Great Mouse Detective" were a key reference point! 

There is also inspiration from adventure films e.g. “The Goonies” and “Pirates of the Caribbean”, and the golden age of Lucas Arts games, such as "Grim Fandango" or "Day of the Tentacle". We love the “Monkey Island” series in particular! 

Although it is true that it is a pirate game at heart, after playing for a few hours, you’ll begin to realize the omnipresence of Irish mythology and folklore. This is something that will be accentuated as you explore the island. 

Although we took a few liberties, there are many historical and mythological references throughout the game and easter egg hunters will find many reasons to explore every inch of the map that we have prepared for them. 

[b]Q: How did you go about designing the environments?[/b] 

[b]Júlia:[/b] As for the environments themselves, we have employed a principle called "navigation by color key". This method uses color palettes to help connect players to the story, environments, and the characters in a coherent way. 

We started with an environmental color palette of blue and teal on Shipwreck Beach, and as the player progresses, the environmental color palettes gradually become more fantastical in tone. If for example you look at The Necromancer’s boss room, we wanted to emphasize and accent the boss character’s pink eldritch magic, so you will see complementary tones appearing throughout the environment and creating a nostalgic 80s high fantasy look and feel. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1d4121b60eb8863f21dfeb35bf5756745e1cbef8.png[/img]

[b]Xavi:[/b] When we faced The Necromancer section during development, we had a stable and defined area of the map with a specific color and a purpose. In this part of the game there are many dank dungeon rooms that give off foreboding vibes… For the boss room itself we suddenly had to convey something different, and that's where concept art and Júlia’s work was invaluable. 

Concept Art is all a matter of perspective: As a first step you have the global point of view of the entire map that goes by color key. But then you get to the next stage of thinking “What's going on in this particular room? Do I have to suddenly change that color to convey something different?”. The creation of key rooms such as this takes a lot of extra planning and thought!

[b]Júlia:[/b] In concept art, we document everything that needs to be reflected in the room, making some first sketches of what the room would be like, and trying different color palettes to get the right fit. This ultimately leads to a finished illustration incorporating all of the different details and assets of the final room, which will then be used for 3D modeling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/c296d68743e6150af01fb4b7dac3727a3f0a6593.png[/img]

[b]Q: Could you explain how you came to the final design of the Necromancer’s boss room?[/b]

[b]Enric:[/b] Every artistic process during development has passed through a multi-departmental pipeline. Our Concept Artists come up with the initial idea and then negotiate with the 3D artists to see if all is possible. 

In the case of Necromancer’s room, this environment changed a lot! Originally it was a grayish room with muted tones and no distinguishable features. Then it was reimagined based on the Necromancer’s design, and greenish and pinkish tones were added to make it feel more mysterious and evil. 
Cauldrons, swords, cobwebs, and knotted tree roots were added to emphasize the fact that the location is deep underground. It turned out pretty cool and the team is proud of what we managed to achieve with this location.

Throughout the entire process, we also had to take into account the fact that at point zero (the area where the character plays) there cannot be any type of object or obstruction. Otherwise, the character would clip through the object, so the cauldron was a headache, as this is where the Necromancer emerges. We actually faked that effect by putting the cauldron in the background and reworking the layout so that the swords and chains didn't interfere with the boss’s animations.

[h3]Composing the original soundtrack with Composer Max Ballet.[/h3] 

[b]Q: How did you approach composing the soundtrack?[/b]

[b]Max:[/b] Starting with the instruments, while strings, piano, winds and percussion feature prominently throughout the soundtrack, there are also few unusual elements such as the harp and even my sister's voice that were used to add subtle details to many of the tracks. 

The piano stands out from all the instruments used because the piano is the instrument on which I was trained: I studied classical piano at the Liceu Conservatory and I have always carried it with me! So, Curse of the Sea Rats has been a project crafted using this instrument. I first composed all the songs on the piano before I transferred them to a digital workflow.

With the wind instruments, the flute has a prominent role in the soundtrack. This is an instrument with a sweet sound that creates a degree of sentimentality and a more human touch. Also, the flute was introduced in such a way that it registers lower and deeper than normal, which is why it still sounds a little sweeter. I have used it in areas where the environment is calm, where you want to give the player a little more peace, conveying serenity with all threats removed. 

At the opposite end of the spectrum, we have the strings, which are the most present instruments during the intense boss battles. During these fights, the strings act as the base, giving weight and body to the composition. The strings intensely convey emotion, making the player feel stronger and more engaged at faster tempos. 

The percussion is also key here, with a degree of primitiveness that gives the boss battle music its strength and urgency. This is particularly apparent with the tracks for the later bosses which are far more dangerous! Percussion barely features during moments of exploration, so this provides a striking contrast.  

[b]Q: Is there one particular track that you really loved working on?[/b]

[b]Max:[/b] One boss track that I really liked, aside from the battle with Flora, was that of the Lighthouse Keeper. In that battle, the music had to represent this character, something strong, something big!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/49eb55082facbd4e9ae13b4e0475e0e6fb238a1d.png[/img]

It’s worth noting that the more diminutive bosses such as Rama and Sharpie have more agile and lighter music. This allows the player to truly feel the speed of each character and adapt a little more to their attack patterns and movement. With the larger bosses, the music had to feel heavier, colder, and more gigantic! 

For example, with the Lighthouse Keeper, we used a lot of percussion to accentuate his tremendously heavy attacks. It feels like tons of stones are falling on the player throughout this fight, and this sensation is ultimately achieved using percussion. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/9875885dcaecf53d6161cd6b24fa992a9f198461.gif[/img]

[b]Q: Do you have any favorite tracks?[/b]

[b]Max:[/b] I really like The Curse which plays during the start screen. This is where the whole journey begins and where one of the most important leitmotifs of the game comes from. 

Other favorites include The Sea Rats which was composed to represent the four heroes, a short Minuet, (which is a baroque dance) that accompanies Flora Burn's abduction of Admiral Blacksmith’s son, and the End Credits theme that embodies a sense of salvation and ultimate victory.

Curse of the Sea Rats has been a perfect game for me to work on, as it strongly incorporates classical music. The game is set in the year 1777, where classicism is at its height in Europe and Mozart is just 21 years old (David Douglas and Mozart even have the same ponytail!). 

It’s also worth noting the importance of Irish folk music in the soundtrack. Its lose, rural character had to blend seamlessly with the precision and perfection of classical music, which was quite a challenge! 

Curse of the Sea Rats launches on [b]6th April 2023![/b] We’ll be back with part 2 of our developer interview series soon!

Until next time!

Watch out Sea Rats!  

Big news incoming, as we can finally reveal that [b][i]Curse of the Sea Rats[/i][/b] will launch on 6th April 2023! To celebrate, we have a brand-new trailer showcasing some of many intense [b]boss battles[/b] you’ll be tackling during your adventure.  

The wicked [b]Captain Flora Burn[/b] has deployed her crewmates at various key locations to hinder your progress. Hand-picked by Flora herself, these devilish pirates have earned their fearsome reputation, one way or another...  

On top of this, the local wildlife has been transformed by the [b]fiendish magic[/b] of the Pirate Witch, with some creatures mutating into monstrous behemoths who will present a serious threat to would-be adventurers.   

Check out some of the more ruthless members of Flora’s crew as well as the other dangers that lurk along the [b]Irish Coast[/b] in our [b]new Boss Trailer[/b]!

As if dangerous swashbucklers, weren’t bad enough, strange creatures like [b]Krabawaki & King Clapper[/b] have also crawled out of the woodwork, lured by the promise of power and riches.

[*] Lex Sharp as the Lighthouse Keeper. 
[*] Marine D’Aure as Rama Cinnamon.

Explore an intriguing setting full of secrets to uncover, diabolical enemies to combat and challenging bosses to overcome when [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] launches on 6th April 2023!

notes.title: Dangers of the Irish Coast
notes.content:
In our last update, we looked at some of the locations you’ll be travelling to during your adventure. As you pursue the wicked Pirate Witch, [b]Flora Burn[/b], you’ll need to work your way through the hordes of enemies she has left in her wake!  

By transforming everyone onboard the [b]HMS Barfleur[/b] into rats, Flora was able to kidnap [b]Admiral Blacksmith’s son [/b]and make her escape to the Irish shore! To ward off any would-be pursuers, Flora has corrupted much of the native plant and animal life, creating malformed and dangerous creatures… 

[h3]Giant. Enemy. Crab. [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/ddae8faa50d3d40aac0fa71a6f36a752a4205cea.gif[/img]

Before you’ve even managed to step off [b]Shipwreck Beach[/b] you’ll come face to claw with [b]Armoured Crabs[/b]. These enemies come in several shapes and sizes but the ones to look out for are the larger, tougher, ones. With hard shells and sharp pincers, the crabs will make short work of anyone that gets too close; however, a [b]well-timed parry[/b] will stun the killer crustacean allowing you to strike its softer underbelly.  

[h3]A Sticky Situation… [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/d55d005d1b6c9652597de96a6d1239b1967bed7e.gif[/img]

Venturing further inland you’ll eventually climb to the heights of [b]Eriu’s Forest[/b]. This lush woodland may seem peaceful at first, but it is filled with vicious insects and plants ready to strike. Hidden among the branches are the large [b]Caterpillars[/b], gargantuan bugs that can [b]birth smaller offspring[/b] to attack intruders. Be careful not to get webbed in the [b]Caterpillar’s sticky silk[/b] or risk being swarmed. 

[h3]To the bat cave! [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/d111f308aa33599705e616eaf199423ef1ebbc5b.gif[/img]

If the forests are too much, try delving down into the deep caves of the [b]Flying Rat’s Hole[/b]. As the name suggests, the caverns are brimming with [b]Giant Bats[/b] ready to swoop in on unsuspecting victims. Don’t rely on the cave walls to protect you as the bats can manoeuvre their way through obstacles before unleashing a [b]lightning-fast dive bomb[/b]!  

[h3]Precarious heights [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/3c092e3da90a3435e4d281bfc5e6982adb41b2e2.gif[/img]

Make it out of the caves alive and you may find yourself clinging to the [b]Cliff of the Winds[/b]. The harsh winds and narrow platforms are made even more treacherous by the [b]mischievous Puffins[/b]. Despite their adorable appearance, these puffins will take any chance they can get to [b]knock you off a ledge[/b] onto the rocky shore below.  

[h3]Hard shells[/h3] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/797aa8ba39be343d4d563634d2c43549f7ae4ffd.gif[/img]

Below the gorgeous orange canopy of [b]Banba’s Forest[/b] lurk some incredibly tough [b]Giant Beetles[/b] that can be difficult obstacles to overcome. Their hard exoskeletons render them [b]impervious to most attacks[/b]. You’ll either need to whip around to their rear or [b]execute a timely parry[/b] when they come rolling towards you.  

[h3]Grave of the fireflies [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/534b14f9067d1f5233150e15f4e87460170aeecd.gif[/img]

Somewhere just below the surface of the Irish Coast lies the [b]Moonlight Lough[/b], a beautifully colourful cave system filled with dew-covered grass and flowing rivulets. Don’t get distracted by the enchanting view or you may fall victim to the [b]explosive Fireflies[/b] that lurk in the shadows. Tread carefully as the deceptively glowing bugs can seemingly [b]vanish without a trace[/b], one wrong move and you’ll face a [b]mighty explosion[/b] that may even trigger a chain reaction.  

That’s all for now, there are still plenty of dangers to uncover on your journey to defeat Flora Burn. Stay tuned for more announcements soon!

notes.title: Exploring the Irish Coast
notes.content:
[h2]Land ho![/h2]

Shake off your sea legs and prepare to explore the Irish Coast as we take a sneak peak at some of the many locations you’ll be traversing in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats! [/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f681289f7ae69bf102b5796c48938784fb00eaa3.png[/img]

Shipwrecked on the rocky shores of this strange land, you’ll soon discover a host of intriguing environments brimming with dangerous enemies, and treasures to uncover!   

[h3]The storm-lashed coast[/h3]

You’ll begin your adventure on the aptly named [b]Shipwreck Beach[/b], where you’ll need to wade through waves of pirates and beasts that Flora has rallied to her cause. You’ll also find many friendly faces by the wreck of the [b]HMS Barfleur[/b] where [b]Admiral Blacksmith[/b] and his crew are busy making repairs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/c64ef39b1b5bf4667365f7f810075fe198f357da.jpg[/img]

Make sure to visit [b]Major Mallory[/b] to learn from his many years of fighting experience or head up to Quartermaster [b]Robert Garfield’s[/b] shop to buy some much-needed supplies.

[h3]A haven of calm[/h3]

Venture far enough through the labyrinthine caves surrounding Shipwreck Beach and you’ll eventually work your way up to the verdant pastures of [b]Molly’s Warehouse[/b]. In stark contrast to the rugged shoreline, Molly’s quaint dwelling is a welcoming site! Here the hardworking Molly and venerable [b]Granny Malone[/b] raise their livestock in peace and comfort, a scenic respite from an otherwise harsh and unforgiving environment!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/9612006bb8e156869a8d65d2c6c4734659820181.jpg[/img]

[h3]Forest of mystery[/h3]

Situated high on the cliffs overlooking the Irish Sea, gnarled trees envelop ancient ruins in the mysterious [b]Eriu’s Forest[/b]. This verdant locale is home to a variety of carnivorous plants, vicious insects, and even camouflaged pirates!   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/06d866d29a9f91d37315c8efad5c2037ea378761.png[/img]

With branches and bark jutting out across the landscape, you’ll need to be light on your feet to navigate the area safely and avoid a long, perilous fall! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/643a23ed9e4d303bc9e039def1601dd3b81aa7bd.gif[/img]

[h3]Into the spider’s web[/h3]

Deep beneath the roots of Eriu’s Forest, lie the nightmarish, cobwebbed burrows of the [b]Spider’s Nest[/b]. It will be easy to get lost in the tangled tunnels so you’ll need to bring a reliable source of light to guide you through the overwise pitch-black environment! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f8f2fd144ab10146bc042898309f5a1a58365b2b.gif[/img]

Filled with scuttling, eight-legged monstrosities you’ll also need to ensure that you have a plentiful supply of antidote vials to combat the potent arachnoid venom…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/2e28d5bd479dc491abf410e095e3a79b65738ca8.jpg[/img]

There are plenty more dangerous and mysterious locations to uncover along the Irish Coast and we can’t wait for you to discover these when [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] launches in [b]early 2023![/b] 

Until next time,

Petoons Studio

[url=https://discord.com/channels/707335419167113217/956597128090750996][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/7546763a75a38c09ff4c709bc05e0f68fa296629.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Boss Spotlight: Rama Cinnamon
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy Sea Rats! [/h2]

We’re back with another Boss spotlight for [b][i]Curse of the Sea Rats[/i][/b] with a close look at another of [b]Flora’s wicked crew[/b]. 

Flora Burn has truly sailed to the ends of the Earth gathering the most vicious pirates from all four corners to help in her quest for power. One such pirate, [b]Rama Cinnamon[/b], likes to think of herself as a strategic genius and likes to taunt her foes. 

Armed with a [b]whip and her wit[/b], Rama sits atop the very apex of [b]Erui’s forest[/b], lying in wait for the Sea Rats. Unlike Sharpie, Rama holds no sense of comradery or sportsmanship towards the Sea Rats and relishes the thought of fighting! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/781941a292505de9cec532a2c4a53896f902bd92.png[/img]

[h3]Goddess on the Mountain Top [/h3]

You’ll need to climb all the way to the top of Erui’s Forest to face off against Rama. Standing in your way is a whole swath of Flora’s troops as well as some of the [b]strangest bugs[/b] and insects to inhabit the land. 

Fight your way through [b]pirates[/b], and [b]beetles[/b], and[b] laser slugs[/b] (oh my!) across the vast overgrown trees. Like the [b]Cliff of the Winds[/b], you’ll need to be quick on your feet to traverse the [b]dense jungle-like area[/b]. 

As you reach the summit be cautious, Rama has set [b]several traps[/b] lying in wait for you… 

[h3]Five Lashes Be Owed [/h3]

Using her whip, Rama has some [b]incredible reach[/b] with her attacks as she cracks it down on the exposed branch arena. Get too close to her and she’ll her [b]acrobatic skills[/b] to leap around and gain as much ground between the both of you as possible.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/2ea3c3ee42404bae4c71491a7aba524260274aae.gif[/img]

Occasionally, she’ll leap into the air and unleash a [b]flurry of whip strikes[/b] that envelop the immediate area. Even without her whip. she can deal some serious damage as she [b]spins violently[/b] and gracefully back and forth. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f7e3d6a731e37274cd49e286e87db3aece242778.gif[/img]

As with many of Flora’s crew, Rama possesses some [b]supernatural powers[/b]. In Rama’s case, she can [b]control vines[/b] and the fauna surrounding her causing [b]waves of thorns[/b] and deadly plants to chase the player. 

Good luck in facing Rama and the rest of [b]Flora’s crew[/b]! There are plenty of other creeps and creatures to uncover on the coast of Ireland, if ye dare… 

Petoons Studio

notes.title: Boss Spotlight: Sharpie the Sharp
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back, shipmates![/h2]

By now, you’ve gotten to know a few of the devilish scoundrels that make up [b]Flora Burn’s crew[/b] in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats.[/b][/i] Following on from the spotlights for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3300598937398284342][b]Fatso[/b][/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/6455372478695200607][b]Murat Reis[/b][/url], we’re here to introduce you to the next pirate challenger, [b]Sharpie the Sharp.[/b]

Sporting two curved blades, Sharpie certainly lives up to her name. However, unlike the rest of Flora’s gang, Sharpie is nothing if not empathic, recognising the plight of the heroes as [b]she too was once a prisoner of the British Empire…[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f9c96f18519d9f3dd6aab579d05d1015fa34a2be.png[/img]

[h3]You didn’t fall? Inconceivable![/h3]

You’ll need to be fast on your feet if you hope to chase down Sharpie the Sharp. Located deep in a forlorn and remote area of the [b]Cliff of the Winds[/b], Sharpie is well within her element. 

With [b]harsh winds[/b] attempting to upset the balance of anyone foolish enough to descend its treacherous cliffside, the narrow platforms hold little comfort for anyone caught off-guard. If that wasn’t enough, Flora has placed [b]several marksmen [/b]in strategic locations to take down any pursuers, taking pot-shots whenever you are at your most vulnerable.

Keep an ear out for the enraged cries of the [b]local puffin population[/b] as well. Once they see someone encroaching on their territory they’ll dive, beak first, at intruders to protect their eggs!

[h3]You Seem a Decent Fellow[/h3]

Once you’ve successfully manoeuvred your way down the cliffside and braced the icy winds, Sharpie will be waiting to stop you in your tracks.

Unlike her crewmates, Sharpie is more willing to embrace you as a fellow prisoner and openly welcomes you into the folds of Flora’s crew! Your refusal to join her however will soon eradicate any initial good-will she had towards you…

A pirate through and through, Sharpie is perhaps the [b]deadliest swordsman on the island.[/b] She is precise, swift, and deadly at all ranges as she hurls razor-sharp gusts of air from her blades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/5787c0f2b70e4f46754da84abfc14b2549f8f565.gif[/img]

Capable of harnessing the harsh winds that whip around her, Sharpie utilises the cliffs to create the perfect offence and defence. Avoid getting close for too long as Sharpie can surround herself with a [b]damaging vortex![/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/de3ef02ec7f6b991ce71fd025c16b6c4586ce37e.gif[/img]

Stray too far, however, and Sharpie will unleash her [b]lightning-fast lunge attack[/b]. Disappearing for a moment, Sharpie will leap forwards, cutting anything in her path into ribbons.

Will you be nimble enough to survive the Cliff of the Winds, and Sharpie’s relentless attacks?

Stay tuned for more boss highlights coming soon!

Petoons Studio

notes.title: Boss Spotlight: Murat Reis
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy Sea-Rats![/h2]

Welcome back to our [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i] boss rundown! Last time around we showcased the first of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3427824991982240954][b]Flora Burn’s[/b][/url] deadly crew, the brutish bully [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3300598937398284342][b]Fatso.[/b][/url] 

Now we shift our attention to another member of her ruthless gang, the mysterious and cunning vampire rat, [b]Murat Reis.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/62aeefb2f4caccfe184e0ff1e35f0d0e71e9af26.png[/img]

[h3]Bat to the Bone[/h3]

To reach Murat Reis, you’ll need to head down into the depths of [b]Flying Rat’s Hole.[/b] Filled with deadly protruding spikes, a dexterous set of paws will be required to navigate the various tunnels beneath the [b]Shellfish Rocks.[/b]

Once you’ve successfully ducked and dived your way through the first few sections of the cave system, you’ll be faced with the [b]locked door[/b] to Murat’s domain which can only be opened using a [b]special key.[/b] Past this, and descending deeper and deeper, you’ll eventually come face to face with the villainous vampire himself!

[h3]Love at First Bite[/h3]

On top of his impeccable dress sense, Murat Reis possesses a [b]unique set of weapons and vampiric abilities[/b] which make him a formidable foe indeed. 

Upon entering the cavernous lair of Murat Reis you’ll immediately notice the exceptionally tall ceiling. Murat Reis makes good use of this space by [b]flying and levitating.[/b] This may seem daunting to landlubbing sea rats at first, but be sure to sneak in some aerial attacks when you get the chance!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1b72c364934b5d3bda68830090fc23ff32f61cd4.gif[/img]

Murat Reis wields his [b]trusty rapier[/b] with deadly speed, darting from one end of the cave to the other. You’ll need to be quick on your feet if you want to avoid getting caught in his path.

To compliment his sword skills, the vampire rat has the power to [b]command dark magic[/b] which he can use to call forth [b]multiple harmful columns of crimson energy. [/b]Keep an eye on the ground for signs of a bubbling eruption waiting to happen!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/bf8149efadc3f51e6b8876ab12f5d0c3ebff16a2.jpg[/img]

Beware as Murat Reis has one last trick up his sleeve… While you’re busy dodging his fountains of dark magic and rapier blows, he’ll also be trying to hit you with his [b]brace of throwing daggers![/b] You’ll need your wits about you if you want to avoid taking unnecessary damage and overcome this flamboyant foe once and for all. 

We hope you’ve enjoyed learning more about the devilish crew of Flora Burn, but stay tuned as we’ll be back with more boss battle spotlights soon!

notes.title: Boss Spotlight: Fatso
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back sea rats![/h2]

Today we’ll be kicking off [b]a new series of posts[/b] dedicated to showcasing some of the [b]many varied bosses[/b] that you’ll be encountering throughout your mission to save Admiral Blacksmith’s son from the clutches of the wicked Captain Flora Burn! 

Many of these powerful foes are in fact [b]elite members of the pirate-witch’s nefarious crew[/b] tasked with stopping you from achieving your ultimate goal. The very first member of this dastardly bunch is the barrel-tossing, wise-cracking glutton, [b]Fatso.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/67b729924cba0e5491a7973459f7a189e0eb596f.png[/img]

Fatso is a large and intimidating bilge rat who makes up for his lack of speed and table manners with his [b]immense strength![/b] Fatso also happens to love a good party and so carries around [b]a large barrel wherever he goes…[/b]

You’ll find Fatso in the [b]Shipwreck Beach[/b] area, literally blocking your path forwards, so you’ll need to best him in a good old-fashioned scrap if you want to continue your adventure. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/b29c9bc75581de333790962bc95a62b15ba24a34.jpg[/img]

The barrel-toting ruffian has no issue with swinging his weight around. Avoid his [b]big sweeping attacks[/b] or be whacked across the room! Fatso loves to fight but can also get a bit carried away, if you get hit by his [b]body slam attack[/b], he’ll pause and have good belly laugh. Use this window of opportunity to get in a few licks before he composes himself for another swing.

His barrel isn’t just for partying either, during the fight Fatso will shake up the fizzy contents and use the resulting [b]gas explosion[/b] to launch himself towards you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/c34f3214396ee18a40f17a36d9ed5090c258dd3c.gif[/img]

The last thing to watch out for are his smaller, [b]spiked barrels[/b] which he hurls across the floor. Only the nimblest of Sea Rats will have a chance of avoiding these so [b]get ready to jump![/b]

Stay tuned as we explore what other dangers lurk along the Irish Coast in our next update…

notes.title: Meet the notorious Pirate Witch, Captain Flora Burn!
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back to another update, Sea Rats![/h2]

Today we’ll be introducing [b]Flora Burn[/b], the dreaded Pirate Captain with a flair for the supernatural, and the main antagonist who you’ll be going up against throughout your adventure. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/19c6ef37377814253e52df56e279c20772e66c25.png[/img]

Along with [b]David Douglas[/b], [b]Buffalo Calf[/b], [b]Bussa[/b], and [b]Akane Yamakawa[/b], Flora and her pirate crew are prisoners of the British Empire, being transported to London aboard the [b]HMS Barfleur[/b]. However, during the crossing Flora and her crew hatch a devious plan to escape...

[h3]I Put A Spell on You[/h3]

By channelling magical energy through a piece of the fabled [i][b]Eye of the Serpent[/b][/i], Flora weaves a diabolical curse which transforms everyone on the HMS Barfleur into rats!   

As an insurance policy, Flora [b]kidnaps the Admiral’s son[/b] and begins transforming the local flora and fauna into ferocious adversaries. In desperation, [b]Admiral Blacksmith[/b] offers the remaining prisoners freedom if they rescue his son. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/7073a1559c7e36c7853f686ce1b212c956b4ff9c.jpg[/img]

It’s up to you lead the hunt for Flora, defeat each member of her elite pirate crew and free little [b]Timothy[/b] from the paws of evil...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/4a4ca376df928c8f300749d971b7ce4549658542.jpg[/img]

[h3]Motley Crew[/h3]

Standing in your way are Flora’s vicious crew. Made up of some of the most conniving and deadly pirates to have ever roamed the seven seas, this band of misfits will stop at nothing to prevent you from catching up to their Captain.

Each of these crew members presides over an area of the map, lying in wait for you to spring their trap. From the terrible twins, [b]Fatso & Fatsie[/b], to the sinister spider, [b]Freddy Eightfingers[/b], there are no shortage of menacing foes to encounter.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/1702764399fe4c0468ef9e4b42d8a478cc84261b.jpg[/img]

Defeating the various elite crew members will not only get you one step closer to Flora but will also [b]yield exciting rewards[/b]. Beating the vampiric flying [b]Murat Reis[/b], for example, will unlock the [b]Dash ability[/b]. The nature of each character’s [b]Dash[/b] is unique, so have fun experimenting with everyone’s move set as you progress forwards. 

Intriguingly, every member of Flora’s entourage that you defeat will yield [b]a golden tooth[/b]. What could these mysterious items mean? [b]Collect the set and find out![/b]  
 
[h3]The Eye of the Serpent[/h3]

On the night the curse was unleashed, the Pirate Witch attempted to steal [b]The Eye of the Serpent[/b], a magical, gem-encrusted artefact. However, she only made away with the gem, ensconced within the ring she wears, leaving the rest of the amulet behind. 

Unaware of its true power, Admiral Blacksmith entrusts the amulet to you in the hopes it will aid you in retrieving his son. 

Now, guided by the wise and powerful [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/6020766858248186298][b]Wu Yun[/b][/url], you must stop Flora Burn and her crew from becoming too powerful, retrieve the other half of the artefact, and perhaps learn more about its true nature...

notes.title: Meet Marcos and Amelio, and help uncover buried treasure!
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back Rat-pack![/h2]

In our last post we met [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3349009461975107671][b]Granny Malone[/b][/url] and talked a little bit about the [b]side quests[/b] that you’ll be undertaking for the many and varied characters you’ll be encountering along the [b]Irish Coast[/b] throughout your adventure in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i].

We touched on how some of these characters will unlock new areas of the map, give you key items needed to progress, and provide rewards for fulfilling their (sometimes outlandish) requests! 

[h3]A Monkey’s Island[/h3]

Certain characters even have [b]unique mechanics[/b] associated with their questlines, and today we’ll be looking at [b]Marcos & Amelio[/b], a curious pair who seem to have gotten themselves into a spot of bother thanks to Amelio’s sticky fingers…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/6b8d1e69402500481db278f81d48955295e3f7b7.png[/img]

Like the other prisoners on board the [b]HMS Barfleur[/b], treasure-hunter Marcos and his loyal monkey companion, Amelio, were captured by the British while they were exploring the Caribbean in search of a [b]mysterious figure[/b]…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f617dbc02737e4ab738e2b39207490d2767d04de.jpg[/img]

In the chaos and confusion caused by [b]Flora’s curse[/b], Marcos and Amelio managed to escape their captors! Unfortunately, Amelio seems to have taken to the pirate lifestyle a bit too readily and has begun [b]stealing and burying[/b] just about anything he can lay his paws on. At first, Amelio stole from strangers but has now started [b]hiding Marcos’ belongings[/b] as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/e25763fb6887b180e79d6fc555f8f3f43628eba4.jpg[/img]

Marcos requests that you find and recover all the trinkets that Amelio has buried across the map. In exchange for your aid, Marcos will let you keep anything you dig up that doesn’t belong to him.

[h3]A Ground-breaking Discovery[/h3]

To help unearth the missing belongings, Marcos supplies you with a handy [b]shovel[/b]. Thankfully, Amelio isn’t quite as skilled at burying treasure as he is at stealing it, and as you traverse the Irish coast you’ll occasionally notice [b]small mounds of dirt[/b] with half-buried objects just about visible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/359496c95456faeb05fd82e8ef0a53a12615395d.gif[/img]

By using your shovel, you’ll be able to [b]dig up the hidden treasure[/b], collecting as many as objects as you can find before returning to Marcos and turning in the goods. Found treasure will show up as [i][b]Unearthed Chests[/b][/i] in your inventory until you exchange them with Marcos who will reveal their contents.

notes.title: Discover the Denizens of the Irish Coast
notes.content:
[h2]Avast ye scurvy Sea Rats![/h2]

Now that you’ve become familiar with some of the main characters in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats[/b][/i], it’s time to introduce you to some of the other colourful individuals that you’ll be coming across in your adventure on the mysterious [b]Irish Coast.  [/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/e3a4d67a15c29c04c22cbd70c268cee4819bfb69.png[/img]

Throughout your mission to recover [b]Admiral Benjamin Blacksmith’s son[/b] from the clutches of [b]Flora Burn[/b], you’ll encounter many other crew members from the [b]HMS Barfleur[/b], nefarious pirates, and even locals of the island. Many of these individuals will need assistance in finding specific items. Help them out to receive a reward which will aid you in your ongoing quest!

[h3]Spice Up Your Life[/h3]

With the crew of the HMS Barfleur now stranded and scattered along the Irish Coast, [b]many require the bare essentials[/b] that have since been claimed by the sea. For example [b]Landsman Rogers[/b] can’t even enjoy his slimy squid snack without the [b]proper seasoning[/b]! Keep an eye out for some 'Black Pepper' and bring it back to this poor cephalopod connoisseur.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/20c8bd11f53de983f94fe177bf34806372d8f159.png[/img]

The Landsman Rogers quest has a fairly simple solution but you’ll find that some characters have some far more involved requests. Take [b]Rick[/b], for instance, he’s in need of a makeover to help blend in with the other pirates on the island. Scour the entire map to help gather a multi-item [b]Pirate Costume[/b] for him!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/eda648fad78dc4f889cd29b7da3acd61afe20460.png[/img]

It’s always worth going the extra mile as each completed side quest will offer you a chance to obtain valuable [b]consumables[/b], unique [b]character enhancements[/b], and even [b]key items[/b]. 

[h3]All’s Wool That Ends Wool[/h3]

Completing some side quests will be essential for progressing through the story as they provide invaluable tools or allow you to open up new areas for exploration. These quests may require key items found around the map or sold by [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/3374903257107252702][b]Robert Garfield[/b][/url], the ship’s Quartermaster.

A good example of this would be [b]Granny Malone[/b] who can be found at [b]Molly’s Farm[/b] early in the game. This sweet old lady is one of the locals who has built her life on the island with her family. Together they run a sheep farm which would be lovely, except that it stands directly between you and your goal… In exchange for some appropriate materials from which to knit a special scarf, Granny Malone with give you her key to Molly’s workshop and unlock a new path forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/4354b8ede956b48b0e2ad991df25b16ef95847fa.png[/img]

Aside from the handful of characters that we’ve mentioned you’ll discover that there are plenty more buccaneers, swashbucklers, and downright bilge rats to be found and dozens of stories to uncover in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats.[/b][/i] 

Thanks for dropping by! We’ll be back soon with another update soon.

notes.title: Meet Robert Garfield, Purveyor of fine and exotic wares!
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy ship(wreck) mates![/h2]

For far we’ve introduced each of the [b]four playable heroes[/b], as well as their mystical guide, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1453900/view/6020766858248186298][b]Wu Yun, Emissary of the Shen![/b][/url] Today we’ll be taking our first look at another member of the [i][b]HMS Barfleur’s[/b][/i] rugged crew, [b]Quartermaster Robert Garfield.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/0239f345e3999ec2427a6b6a03e1de6e568e95de.png[/img]

Setting up shop in one of the many coastal caves along [b]Shipwreck Beach[/b], Robert manages the ship’s supplies with his assistant [b]Wallace[/b], ensuring that everything is accounted for and rationed accordingly. 
 
[h3]The Rat of Wallstreet[/h3]

While Wallace is busy [strike]snoozing[/strike] fixing up the bridge to open a new path forwards, Robert runs the shop offering up merchandise, for a price… After all, with supplies in short supply and high demand, Robert can’t just go giving things away for free! Instead he’ll ask that you pay for his wares using standard pirate currency, [b]Gold.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f139ddcaf41ec06ab53f2d80ee53321f59a52bdf.jpg[/img]

There are several ways to acquire Gold in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats.[/b][/i] The first, and most straightforward method is by [b]defeating enemies.[/b] Most foes will drop a small quantity of treasure that you’ll gradually accumulate over time. Beware though as [b]not all enemies will have deep pockets,[/b] so there’s no guarantee that you’ll come away any richer from every fight!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/f5402b2b0916194d2e5b1ce7868128f3b13d18e9.gif[/img]

The second method is by [b]discovering and opening chests[/b] that are spread across the map. Some chests can be found in plain site, while other are deviously hidden… Watch out for[b] booby-trapped chests[/b] that contain a nasty surprise!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/38fcf387c6be34caffe390371804ec273a484216.gif[/img]

The best thing about Gold is that unlike [b]Spiritual Energy[/b], you’ll retain all your hard-earned loot even when defeated!

[h3]Quis Est Iste Qui Venit?[/h3]

Much of what Robert sells will be invaluable in your quest as you tackle the dangerous crew of pirate witch, [b]Flora Burn.[/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/ccace52ed9d2c81538c97a0bfea1b1d8c8e7fc84.jpg[/img]

From [b]Health and Energy Nostrums[/b] that keep your heroes fighting fit, to the humble [b]Return Whistle[/b], which transports your party back to the Quartermaster’s location, Robert has plenty of intriguing single use and consumable items available. He also stocks a reserve of rarer items such as [b]Spotless Mind Tonic[/b] that resets an individual’s skill tree and returns all spent Spiritual Energy back to your inventory, just the thing if you feel like changing your approach to a new challenge. 

It’s worth noting that your heroes can only [b]hold a limited quantity of each consumable item.[/b] So, if you’re gearing up for a gruelling boss battle, you’ll need to be careful to preserve your stock of precious healing items as you make your way to a bosses’ area.

It remains a mystery as to how Robert was able to get hold of some of his more well… unusual items, but it’s always worth considering the breadth of what he has to offer as [b]certain curios might come in handy,[/b] particularly when you encounter certain characters further inland.   

[h3]I Know a Shortcut![/h3]

There are plenty of other interesting items, consumables, and collectables to find during your adventure. [b]Cups of Tea,[/b] [b]Sandwiches,[/b] and various other snacks are fairly common, but it’s probably best not to think about how long they’ve been hanging around! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/7567c891765d7ae7be8c909e664d9f7a63c847e0.jpg[/img]

You can prioritise and assign [b]up to four items to the Quick Shortcut menu.[/b] This menu can be accessed on the fly and allows you to quickly gain the upper hand in combat or replenish your health and energy if you find yourself in a sticky situation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39297607/e37d9badb2261877a3d31efc23cfc35f82779766.gif[/img]

Keep an eye out as [b]Robert also likes to move around,[/b] seeking new business opportunities across the map as you blaze a trail forwards!

And so concludes our spotlight on the [i][b]HMS Barfleur’s[/b][/i] amicable Quartermaster! We hope you’ve enjoyed learning more about his role in [i][b]Curse of the Sea Rats,[/b][/i] and feel much better prepared to take on the challenges that lie ahead!

We’ll be back in a few weeks' time with another update, until then!
